tasks.short: Agree the window for repairs and upgrades

steps.what: Log the device, site and wanted window
Check the queue for window clashes
Draft the maintenance order from the form

loop.input: request fields and the clash list
loop.output: order that cites one device id and one window
loop.check: Device id and window match a request row
loop.stop: One draft, then stop; leave the order blank if the device id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: The reason one job should slip is not a fixed field

steps.what: Agree which job takes the window
File the signed window and notify
Report the job done or slipped

tasks.design: Operators submit device id, site, work type and a wanted window on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts the order only from those fields and from clashes on the {CALENDAR}. The architect signs one window version in the meeting, and only that version is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Maintenance asks arrived as free-text mail, so two jobs could book the same device without a shared window record.
tasks.enabler_now: A form can require device id, site and a start time, and the calendar can show overlaps on that device id.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which site waits when two repairs collide is still a call with the people affected.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides which job takes the window and which one slips.

ambition.what: Set maintenance windows every week from the open queue, not when a repair is already late

tasks.altitude: The week moves from chasing status to the clashes. The architect can refuse a window that has no device id or no owner.

reach.task: Do the repair in the filed window
reach.learn: Which window version is signed and which jobs slipped

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this task is a queue plus a meeting. The hard part is which job gets the window, not the notice text.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A maintenance log should record device id, window and result, not staff activity.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and, for firms in scope, the duty of care includes maintenance measures. Sector and size decide scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when a signed window is filed. Doing the repair is the operator's later work.

Input contract: device id, site, work type, wanted start, wanted end, ticket id. Producer is the network operator. If the form is empty the architect types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual.
The prior's small external share is not this task. Vendor dates sit in equipment installation. Use the calendar's own conflict view and the workflow form before custom code.
Native configuration is tested before custom code. Template upkeep is counted in incremental hours.
unknowns: Who may sign a window when the architect is absent.
Whether production changes are frozen outside the agreed window.
Whether this firm is in scope of the Dutch cyber duty of care.
research_questions: What share of jobs last month missed the filed window?
How often do two open jobs name the same device id?

already_counted.description: Architect rewrites a weak order before the meeting
Architect's time choosing which job slips

incremental.description: Keep the work-type list and the order template aligned with new job kinds
Operators correct requests the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: maintenance window version agreed in this meeting
the same signed maintenance window version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes half the jobs still arrive as free text, so the clash list is thin and the meeting does the sorting. The high case assumes clean forms, but every clash is still decided in the meeting. The repair itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Submit site, rack and wanted week
Check rack, power and uplink ids
Draft the equipment installation sheet from the request

loop.output: sheet citing rack id, uplink id and wanted week
loop.check: Every id on the sheet is on the request or the gap list
loop.stop: One draft; leave a blank where the rack id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: Access notes differ by site and are not a fixed merge

steps.what: Agree the week and the access
Confirm the ship date and engineer
Sign the install plan version
File the signed plan and access note

tasks.design: The service owner submits site, rack id, device type and wanted week on a {WORKFLOW} form. The architect checks rack, power and uplink on the {OPS_SYSTEM}, and a bounded sheet in {DOCS} drafts the install plan. The vendor engineer confirms shipment on the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. The architect signs that plan version before anyone is sent the access note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Install dates lived in mail between the vendor and the site, so the rack and the shipment were not one record.
tasks.enabler_now: Rack id, power feed and uplink id can be read from the inventory, and a portal can return a ship date on a request id.
tasks.still_hard: Site access, a late crate and a full rack still need a person to pick a new week.
tasks.human_edge: The architect signs the week only after the rack check and the ship date both exist.

ambition.what: Lock the install week when the request is accepted, not on the day the crate arrives

tasks.altitude: Less time is spent reconstructing the thread. The architect can stop an install that has no rack id or no ship date.

reach.task: Bring the device in the signed week
reach.learn: Which plan version is signed and which access notes are still blank

evidence.claim: Installation coordination in a mid-size firm is a rack check, a vendor date and an access list. The meeting is where the week is chosen.
Digest [S20] and [S21] say product cyber-resilience duties apply to products placed on the market, not to this internal installation.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so this task does not let an unattended step connect the new device.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when the signed install plan is filed. Racking the device is the vendor engineer's work in this same task, not a later project.
Input contract: site, rack id, device type, wanted week, uplink id, request id. Producer is the service owner. Missing rack id or device type is returned to the owner, not invented.
The meeting prior is high and this task keeps it. Use the inventory's own rack fields and the portal's ship-date field before custom code.
unknowns: Which racks have no power or uplink id in the inventory.
Who may sign site access when the architect is away.
Whether the vendor portal exposes a ship date or only a free-text mail.
research_questions: What share of installs last quarter arrived before the rack was free?
How often does the ship date move after the plan is signed?

already_counted.description: Architect edits access notes the draft gets wrong
Meeting time to pick the week stays with the architect

incremental.description: Update the install sheet when a new rack type appears
Vendors resend a ship date when the request id is wrong

approvals.approved_version: install plan version signed after the ship note
the same signed install plan version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes ship dates still arrive as mail and several racks have no ids, so the sheet is mostly retyped. The high case assumes the form and the portal are used, but the week is still chosen in the meeting. Connecting the device is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read link performance and decide capacity

steps.what: Read link counters and error rates
Flag links over the set threshold
Draft the capacity note from flagged links

loop.input: breach rows and the note template
loop.output: note that cites only those link ids
loop.check: Every cited link id is on the breach list
loop.stop: One draft; drop any sentence with no link id
loop.why_not_simpler: Why a busy hour is or is not real demand is not a lookup

steps.what: Decide which links need more capacity
File the signed capacity note

tasks.design: Link id, utilisation, error rate and the agreed threshold sit on a {BI} view fed from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A fixed rule flags rows over the threshold. A bounded note in {DOCS} cites only those link ids. The architect decides which links to grow. This task does not change the live network.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counters were copied into a spreadsheet by hand, so a note could not show which link and which hour it used.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitoring can export link id, utilisation and error rate as rows a threshold can test.
tasks.still_hard: A busy hour may be a one-off, and only the architect can say whether the link should grow.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides which threshold breaches are real demand and which can wait.

ambition.what: Review capacity from a weekly threshold list instead of a quarterly spreadsheet

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to assembling counters. The architect can ignore a note that cites a link id not on the export.

reach.task: Accept or defer a capacity request
reach.learn: Which links the architect has already marked for growth and which are only busy hours

evidence.claim: Capacity work in a mid-size firm is counters plus a judgement. The meeting share in the prior overstates a task that sits on the monitor and the note.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. This view keeps link counters and does not name a person.
A threshold flag is only as good as the link id on the row. Rows without that id still have to be read by hand.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed capacity note. Changing the link size is a later task.
Input contract: link id, utilisation percent, error rate, hour, threshold, site. Producer is the monitoring export. Rows with no link id are left off the flag list.
The meetings prior is about a fifth of the time. For this task the time is the monitor, the export and the note. Use the monitoring view's own threshold before custom code.
If a later design added user identity to the same view, that would be a different task and would need a works-council check. This one does not.
unknowns: Which links have no stable id in the export.
Whether a busy hour is already explained by a known maintenance window.
research_questions: What share of export rows lack a link id?
How often is a flagged link left unchanged after review?

already_counted.description: Architect rewrites note lines that overstate a busy hour
Capacity judgement stays with the architect

incremental.description: Retune thresholds and the note template when a new link type appears

approvals.approved_version: capacity decision signed for these link ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most rows have no link id, so the flag rarely fires and the architect still sorts the export. The high case assumes clean rows, but every growth decision stays manual. No bandwidth change is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Copy network device rows into the document
Draft the prose from the device rows

loop.input: device rows and the template sections
loop.output: prose that cites only those device ids
loop.check: Every device id in the draft is on the device table
loop.stop: One draft; leave a section blank when its device id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: Site-specific warnings are not a fixed mail merge

steps.what: Sign the document version
File the signed document version
Confirm the document matches the service

tasks.design: The document template in {DOCS} reads device id, site and role from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, so the old hand copy stops. A bounded draft writes the prose and may cite only those device ids. The architect signs one version. Owner and date fields can still be wrong, so the sign-off reads them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents were copied from the last site, and the device list in the file drifted from the inventory.
tasks.enabler_now: Inventory rows can feed a template by device id, and a draft can be checked for ids that are not on that list.
tasks.still_hard: The sentences that say how a site actually works still need the architect.
tasks.human_edge: The architect accepts or rejects the prose and the version that gets filed.

ambition.what: File a new document version after each accepted network change, not at the yearly tidy-up

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to pasting device tables. The architect can refuse a version that cites an unknown device id.

reach.task: Confirm the document matches the service
reach.learn: Which document version is current and which device rows were left blank

evidence.claim: Network documentation in a mid-size firm is a device list plus prose. The prior's meeting share overstates a task that is mostly the document.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong. That covers owner and date, not the body of the document.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when a signed document version is filed. It does not include writing a new design.
Input contract: device id, site, role, owner, document type. Producer is the inventory export. If a device id is missing, that row is left blank and the prose for it is not drafted.
The meetings prior does not fit. Time today is the document and the inventory screen. Use the document store's own template and approval flow before custom code.
unknowns: Which document types have no template yet.
Who may sign when the architect is absent.
Whether retired devices remain in the inventory export.
research_questions: What share of filed documents cite a device id that is not in the inventory?
How many document types are still free text?

already_counted.description: Architect rewrites site warnings in the draft
Sign-off time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Add a template section when a new document type appears
Service owners send back comments on a wrong site name

approvals.approved_version: network document version signed in this review
the same signed network document version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many devices have no stable id, so the hand copy remains and the draft is short. The high case assumes the template is linked, but every prose section and every sign-off stay with the architect. No design work is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less of the week goes to status chasing and recopied notes. Window clashes, capacity calls and documents that cite the wrong device still sit with the architect.
reach: Network operators take the filed maintenance window as the queue, instead of a mail thread.
Service owners can read the signed capacity note and the current document version.
skills_to_grow: Write a maintenance window as a device id, a start and an owner.
Separate a capacity threshold from the decision to add bandwidth.
Keep a document version tied to the inventory ids it cites.
role.ambitious_version: Each site shows a current maintenance window, a capacity note and a document set that use the same device ids.
